episodes.203139: A new multi-day plume of monsoon moisture advected northward into New Mexico between an upper level trough over the southern Baja Peninsula and an upper high over the south-central CONUS. Daily rounds of afternoon thunderstorms producing heavy rain developing over the mountains of New Mexico before moving over surrounding lower elevations through the evening resulted in several events of flash flooding and isolated reports of large hail. Rainfall rates of 4 inches per hour totaling 2 inches in 30 minutes produced flash flooding in Magdalena on July 20th. The Cochiti Golf Course experienced flash flooding July 21st. The highest coverage of thunderstorms during this period occurred July 22nd with thunderstorms moving over the Ruidoso area burn scars just after sunset. Flash flooding and debris flows on and below the South Fork and Salt burn scars resulted in brief road closures. The Albuquerque metro experienced flash flooding from heavy rainfall rates of 2 inches per hour totaling 1 to 1.50 inches in 30 minutes over the North Valley neighborhood. Finally, thunderstorms producing heavy rainfall on July 24th directly over the South Fork burn scar totaling just over 2 inches produced flash flooding and debris flows down Cedar Creek and the Rio Ruidoso to Ruidoso Downs.
episodes.203231: Abundant moisture and instability led to the development of scattered thunderstorms across Middle Tennessee on July 22, 2025. One particular thunderstorm near Lawrenceburg downed several trees in the area.
episodes.203257: Multiple clusters of storms moved across portions of central, north central and northeast South Dakota on the morning of July 23rd. Many of these storms produced strong winds and wind related damage. A peak wind gust of 80 mph was observed by the South Dakota State University mesonet station near Lower Brule, while a peak wind gust of 76 mph was measured by the South Dakota Department of Transportation weather station two miles south of Lowry. Thunderstorm winds were also responsible for damage grain bins and the Agtegra building near the town of Carpenter. Three boaters required rescue when their boat capsized on Dry Lake due to thunderstorm winds.
episodes.203260: A push of monsoon moisture into southeast Wyoming lead to the development of widespread showers and storms that eventually converged over the city of Cheyenne. Intense rainfall lead to impressive rainfall rates, resulting in urban flooding across the city.
episodes.203450: A line of thunderstorms and a few supercells developed ahead of a warm front Wednesday (7/23) afternoon across central and north-central Wisconsin. The storms eventually developed into a Quasi-Linear Convective System and tracked through the rest of central, east-central, and northeast Wisconsin through the early evening.  The strongest storms produced damaging winds and 5 tornadoes.
episodes.203517: A line of thunderstorms produced strong winds over the bay of Green Bay and Lake Michigan during the evening hours on Wednesday (7/23).
episodes.204065: An upper ridge over the Southeast led to very warm temperatures. Additionally, localized surface convergence allowed isolated convection to occur.  High precipitable values over 2 inches caused heavy rainfall with the convection, resulting in an isolated instance of flash flooding in Leesville, SC.
episodes.204148: In the afternoon of the 23rd, a supercell developed in southwestern Nebraska and produced one inch hail in southwestern Red Willow county.
episodes.204149: In the afternoon of the 23rd, a supercell developed in Southwestern Nebraska before moving into Northwestern Kansas. As this storm moved into Kansas, additional storms popped up nearby the first one. These storms produce hail up to nickel size in Kansas.
episodes.204340: Scattered thunderstorms spread northeast out of northwest Oklahoma during the afternoon. The storms produced a few severe wind gusts.
episodes.204605: A deeply mixed planetary boundary layer and a mid-level monsoon moisture plume streaming overhead contributed to scattered thunderstorm development late in the afternoon on the 22nd. A relatively dry lower level atmosphere allowed a few of these storms to become severe producing severe wind gusts.
episodes.205047: Although most showers and thunderstorms associated with an upper-level disturbance remained over the open Caribbean waters on July 23rd, showers affected parts of eastern and northern Puerto Rico this morning and to afternoon. One flooding report was received from Fajardo.
episodes.205206: Severe storms moved across northeastern Minnesota the morning of the 23rd ahead of a cold front. Storms began in Cass County where they produced tree damage and a measured gust of 64 mph in Walker. As they moved to the northeast, they lost their strength, but became heavy rain producers which led to some minor flooding in the city of Ely during the late morning hours.
episodes.205208: Thunderstorms moved across the region during the morning of the 23rd ahead of a cold front. While the storms were not severe as they reached northwestern Wisconsin, they were producing heavy rainfall. State Highway 35 through Siren was covered by water during the late morning hours following the storms leading to minor traffic issues.
episodes.205256: Slow morning thunderstorms producing heavy rainfall resulting in flash flooding and closed streets in Bemidji, MN during the morning hours. Tree damage debris from the June 20-21 derecho contributed to blocked storm drains and exacerbated street flooding.
episodes.205475: A small cluster of thunderstorms developed in central Iowa in unstable airmass and moved into the area before midnight  This storm produced damaging winds as the storms moved through Independence.
episodes.205482: Thunderstorms that develop late in the evening on July 22nd moved into Buchanan County around midnight and continue into the early morning hours. A warm and humid airmass led to heavy rain. The heavy rain led to flash flooding north of Winthrop in Buchanan County.
episodes.205552: Two areas of storms developed during the evening hours and continued into the overnight in north central and south central Kansas. Strong and damaging winds were the main hazard with estimated wind gusts up to 75 mph. There was damage to trees and powerlines reported. A semi trailer was blown over on Interstate 70 as well. A few of the storms had hail from nickel to quarter size. These storms were efficient rainfall producers with flooding in the western portions of Saline County which closed many roadways as 7.45 inches fell in Brookville.
episodes.205608: Scattered thunderstorms developed during the early afternoon hours of July 23 across the Sandhills, southwestern and portions of central Nebraska. This activity developed in advance of an approaching cold front. As the afternoon progressed, activity became better organized and severe over Keith County mid afternoon.  As storms tracked east into Lincoln and Custer Counties, they maintained their intensity into the evening hours. A couple of tornadoes were reported in Custer County. Elsewhere, hail up to 2.5 inches in diameter, along with heavy rain and wind gusts up to 60 MPH were reported.
episodes.205618: Afternoon sea breeze convection within south-southeast flow southeast of an area of disturbed weather centered near Apalachee Bay in the northeast gulf produce gusty winds over the Tampa Bay waters.
episodes.205916: A strong thunderstorm passed over Kaycee and produced penny sized hail.
episodes.205990: Dying thunderstorms produced heat burst wind gusts during the late evening and early morning hours. Later afternoon convection produced damaging wind gusts that were detected by SD mesonet stations.
episodes.205996: A strong upper high over the southeast US and a trough approaching the west coast streamed deep moisture into the Borderland with a low level surface trough located through far west Texas into eastern New Mexico.  Slow moving storms brought rainfall amounts of 1 to 3 inches to areas of Dona Ana and Otero counties with the Vado area most significantly impacted.
episodes.205997: A strong upper high over the southeast US and a trough approaching the west coast streamed deep moisture into the Borderland with a low level surface trough located through far west Texas into eastern New Mexico. Slow moving storms brought heavy rainfall and flash flooding to the Anthony and Socorro areas.
episodes.206045: Scattered thunderstorms formed across the southern Texas Panhandle on the evening of July 22nd. The atmosphere was supportive of storms that could produce isolated severe wind gusts up to 70 mph.
episodes.206046: During the late afternoon and early evening of July 23rd, thunderstorms formed over the northeastern Texas Panhandle into the far eastern Oklahoma Panhandle. As these storms moved east to northeast the atmosphere supported strong thunderstorms that could produced severe wind gusts. Some of these thunderstorms produced wind damage that could have resulted from winds up to 80mph.
episodes.206047: During the late afternoon and early evening of July 23rd, thunderstorms formed over the northeastern Texas Panhandle into the far eastern Oklahoma Panhandle. As these storms moved east to northeast the atmosphere supported strong thunderstorms that could produced severe wind gusts. Some of these thunderstorms produced wind damage that could have resulted from winds up to 80mph.
episodes.206078: An area of scattered storms tracked into Douglas County during the evening on July 22nd. One storm produced a downburst of strong winds as its core rapidly collapsed near the Alexandria Regional Airport (KAXN). No damage was reported.
episodes.206079: Several clusters of storms moved from central South Dakota into Minnesota during the morning, then more widespread coverage of storms developed and persisted throughout much of the day. The main axis of heavy rainfall was tied to a slow moving boundary that started across central Minnesota in the morning and progressed towards southern Minnesota by the late evening.||While many locations saw heavy rainfall amounts and rainfall rates at times, two main spots reported flash flooding impacts. This included the city of Albany in Stearns County and the Skyline area just south of Mankato in Blue Earth County. ||There was also an isolated funnel cloud report with a storm that moved through Waseca County that did not produce a tornado.
episodes.206174: A west-to-east oriented broken line of thunderstorms along the South Dakota-Nebraska border near sunrise on July 23 rapidly lifted north the remainder of the morning in response to a strong low-level jet. Damaging wind gusts were observed across portions of Aurora and Beadle Counties with the Huron Regional Airport (KHON) reporting a wind gust of 82 mph. Tree damage was reported across Huron and Plankinton, South Dakota with isolated structural damage in other parts of the area.
episodes.206176: A cluster of thunderstorms erupted within a very moist and unstable airmass ahead of a slow moving frontal boundary during the evening of July 23. These thunderstorms bisected the city of Sioux Falls from southwest to northeast with neighborhoods southeast of I-229 reporting 2 to 5 inches of rain in a matter of 1-2 hours. This resulted in significant flash flooding across impacted portions of the city. Later in the evening, a large mesoscale convective system across Nebraska moved north and east, bringing heavy rain to portions of southeast South Dakota. Additional localized flash flooding was observed after midnight in Beresford, South Dakota.
episodes.206199: A weak surface boundary lingered across the northern Gulf on July 23, 2025, supporting scattered strong thunderstorms over the coastal waters and Mississippi Sound. Several marine observing sites measured strong wind gusts, including 40 mph at the Southwest Pass Pilot Station, 45 mph south of Sand Island, 43 mph at Petit Bois Island, and 53 mph at Keesler AFB. The strongest gust was 59 mph, measured by the Weatherflow mesonet on Ship Island.
episodes.206231: A series of training thunderstorms brought flash flooding to portions of Houghton and Ontonagon Counties between 0300 and 0730EST on July 23. Four-hour rainfall totals ranged from two to four inches in the area. The Governor of Michigan declared a state of emergency as a result of the flooding.
episodes.206239: A cluster of storms which developed on the edge of a low-level jet and east of the main severe weather across South Dakota produced an isolated severe wind gust near Rushmore in the early morning of July 23.
episodes.206254: Thunderstorms moved northward through Pima and Cochise counties and produced heavy rainfall with reported totals ranging from 0.10 to 1.0 inches. The heavy rainfall closed multiple roadways in Tucson, Saint David, Tombstone, and Sierra Vista.
episodes.206388: A few thunderstorms produced hail up to quarter size and gusts up to 58 mph across southeast Montana.
episodes.207438: On July 22nd, Scattered thunderstorms developed across eastern Oregon as an upper level trough moved across the area. Precipitable water values were near the 50th percentile.

This was a very isolated wind gust with no reported damage associated with it. The storm collapsed and dumped what was left of its core over KAXN where the 69 mph gust was measured.

Additionally, an off duty NWS employee observed that the entire south facing roof of a barn was lifted and peeled back near the mesonet location.

Water was reported overtopping Cedar Creek Drive near Sam Tobias Campground, Mechem Drive at Brady Canyon Road, Gavilan Canyon Road north of Sudderth Drive (Highway 70) and Sudderth Drive itself in Hollywood. Some debris flow with a 3 foot wall of mud was also observed on Main Road at McDaniel Drive along with possible evidence of a landslide off Flume Ridge.

Flooding extended into into a backyard and crawl space of a house with an artificial pond washed out about 4 miles east of Tularosa.

A tornado briefly touched down north of Northland at 5:04 PM CDT, moving east-northeast before turning east-southeast and then dissipating at 5:13 PM CDT.  The tornado snapped and uprooted a few trees and produced minor damage to a house. Based on satellite analysis, there may have been a few brief moments where the tornado lifted off the ground before dissipating west of Big Falls. Total path length is estimated to be 5.69 miles long, with a width of 45 yards. Peak wind estimated to be around 75 mph.

A slow-moving thunderstorm dropped an estimated 1 to 1.5 inches of rain in 20 minutes in the North Valley and Los Ranchos de Albuquerque neighborhood of Albuquerque. This resulted in flash flooding on the eastbound lanes of Paseo Del Norte at Rio Grande Blvd and on the westbound frontage road of Paseo Del Norte at Jefferson Street. Additionally, a post on social media reported flood waters entering a business on 4th Street in the Los Ranchos de Albuquerque neighborhood. Finally, a video on social media showed floodwaters in the individual's residence and the family sweeping out the floodwaters from the front entrance of the residence. Property damage cost for the business on 4th street and the residence in the North Valley neighborhood is an estimate.

A tornado briefly touched down south of Clintonville at 5:32 PM|CDT, moving east-northeast before dissipating at 5:34 PM CDT. The tornado was spotted by the local fire department and tracked over mainly open areas with little to no damage indicators. The only damage indicators were disturbances to crops on satellite analysis. Total path length is estimated to be 1.32 miles long, with a width of 80 yards. Path estimated based on radar and satellite imagery.
